name: Lambs Lettuce
family: Caprifoliaceae, the honeysuckle family (formerly the valerian family, Valerianaceae)
grown_as: Corn salad, sown in late summer and picked as whole small rosettes through winter. William's records list the variety 'Vit', a long-leaved, glossy kind.
habit: A neat, flat rosette 8 to 12 cm across and a few cm high. In spring it sends up a slender stem 15 to 30 cm that forks again and again in twos, each fork ending in a small flat cluster of tiny flowers.

leaf.arrangement: Rosette leaves in opposite pairs, crowded; on the flowering stem in opposite pairs at each fork
leaf.outline: Spoon-shaped to oblong (narrow at the base, widest near the rounded end), 2 to 7 cm long
leaf.base: Tapering into a short, winged stalk
leaf.margin: Smooth, without teeth; stem leaves sometimes with one or two small teeth near the base
leaf.veins: A single clear midrib; side veins faint
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless, a little glossy and slightly fleshy
leaf.stalk: Short and winged, merging into the blade

flower.form: A tiny funnel-shaped flower opening into five spreading lobes
flower.petals: Five, joined into a short tube, with five rounded lobes
flower.behind: No sepals that show; small green bracts under each cluster
flower.carried: In small, dense, flat-topped clusters at the tips of the forked stems, facing up
flower.size: About 2 mm across; each cluster 1 to 2 cm

fruit: A tiny flattened, rounded nutlet 2 to 2.5 mm with a corky swelling on one side, pale brown, no hairs or plume. Each holds one seed.
seedling: Two small oval to round seed leaves on short stalks, then a first opposite pair of spoon-shaped true leaves.
winter: Winter is its season: a low green rosette that sits through frost and is picked whole.

leaf: a smooth spoon-shaped leaf with a rounded tip
tapering to a short winged stalk
bloom: a tiny pale lilac-blue flower with five rounded lobes
seed: a tiny rounded flattened pale brown seed 2 mm
seedling: the first true leaves in an opposite pair
young: a small flat rosette of spoon-shaped leaves
crop: a neat flat rosette 8 to 12 cm across
glossy, smooth, spoon-shaped dark green leaves
flower: a slender stem forking again and again in twos
pairs of narrow leaves at the forks
tiny pale blue flowers in flat clusters at the tips
seedhead: tiny round seeds in small clusters at the tips

look_alikes: Other corn salads differ only in their tiny fruits. Seedlings of forget-me-not are hairy and alternate. Young lettuce leaves are thinner, paler and puckered.
